7    INTRODUCTION

8          Q.     Please state your name and business address.

9          A.     My name is Trevor Rucker, and my business address is Missouri Public

10   Service Commission, P.O. Box 360, Jefferson City, MO 65102.

11         Q.     Are you the same Trevor Rucker that filed direct testimony in this case?

12         A.     Yes.

13         Q.     What is the purpose of your surrebuttal / true-up direct testimony?

14         A.     In my surrebuttal / true-up direct testimony, I will discuss 1) the rebuttal

15   testimony of Evergy Missouri Metro (“EMM”) witnesses Ronald A. Klote and Ryan Mulvany

16   regarding Staff’s plant-in-service reporting recommendation, 2) the rebuttal testimony

17   of the Office of the Public Counsel (“OPC”) witness Geoff Marke regarding certain

18   EMM expenditures, 3) Staff’s updated recommendation for plant-in-service reporting,

19   and 4) Staff’s recommended disallowance for costs related to game tables and game

20   table accessories.




                                             Page 1
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1    SURREBUTTAL

2           EMM Rebuttal Testimony

3           Q.     Can you summarize the rebuttal testimony of EMM’s witnesses, Mr. Klote

4    and Mr. Mulvany?

5           A.     Yes. EMM witnesses Mr. Klote and Mr. Mulvany discussed and disagreed

6    with parts of my recommendation to modify the plant-in-service reporting

7    requirements from those in the Stipulation and Agreement approved in Commission

8    Case No. ER-2022-0129 (“ER-2022-0129 Stipulation”).

9           Q.     What are the ER-2022-0129 Stipulation plant-in-service reporting

10   requirements, and what recommendation was included in your direct testimony?

11          A.     The ER-2022-0129 Stipulation plant-in-service reporting requirements are

12   that EMM annually file the following documentation in its capital budget docket

13   (Commission Case No. EO-2019-0047) for projects over $5 million: purchase orders,

14   change orders, final project cost summaries, project justification summary,

15   oversight reviews, and in-service dates.

16          In my direct testimony, Staff’s recommendation was that the plant-in-service

17   reporting requirements be modified so that EMM would quarterly file the following

18   information and documentation in its capital budget docket (Commission Case No.

19   EO-2019-0047) for all projects with an EMM jurisdictional cost over $1 million:

20                 a. Original project cost (total and EMM allocated),
21                 b. Final project cost (total and EMM allocated),
22                 c. In-service date,
23                 d. Project type,


                                                Page 2
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1                   e. Project category,
2                   f. Project description,
3                   g. Project justification summary,
4                   h. Oversight reviews,
5                   i. Purchase orders (including supporting, attached, and referenced
6                      documentation), and
7                   j. Change orders (including supporting, attached, and referenced
8                      documentation).

9           Q.      What parts of your recommendation did EMM’s witnesses disagree with?

10          A.      EMM’s    witnesses     disagreed      with   changing   the   cost   threshold

11   from $5 million to $1 million in EMM jurisdictional cost, and specifying that supporting,

12   attached, and referenced documentation be included with purchase and change orders.

13          Q.      Why did EMM’s witnesses disagree with these changes?

14          A.      EMM’s witnesses primarily disagreed with these changes due to the

15   increased work for EMM. EMM’s witnesses questioned if the additional volume of

16   reporting would be beneficial and improve Staff’s ability to conduct oversight. EMM also

17   stated that Staff’s review of a sample of projects costing between $1 million

18   and $5 million did not identify any patterns of unreasonable or imprudent spending.

19          Q.      Had Staff completed its review of projects costing over $1 million at the

20   time of Staff’s direct testimony filing?

21          A.      No. At the time that Staff’s direct testimony was filed, Staff had just recently

22   received documentation for a sample of projects costing over $1 million.




                                                 Page 3
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1    My direct testimony stated that Staff would continue its review and provide true-up direct

2    testimony if necessary.

3               Q.      Does EMM completely oppose Staff’s recommended modifications to the

4    ER-2022-0129 Stipulation plant-in-service reporting requirements?

5               A.      No. EMM witness Mr. Klote stated that EMM could comply with the

6    reporting requirements proposed by Staff if ordered by the Commission. 1 EMM witness

7    Mr. Klote adds that the issue is not whether EMM can provide the information, but if the

8    benefits justify the increased reporting volume.

9               Q.      What would be the approximate increase in reporting volume?

10              A.      It is important to clarify that EMM has been providing documentation for

11   projects in its capital budget docket filings with costs over $5 million for the EMM

12   allocated portion of the cost. Staff had anticipated that the $5 million cost threshold

13   would be for the total project cost. However, Staff recognizes that the ER-2022-0129

14   Stipulation plant-in-service reporting requirements did not specify if the $5 million cost

15   threshold was for the total project cost or the EMM allocated portion of the cost,

16   which allows for different interpretations of the requirement.

17              Interpreting the $5 million cost threshold as applying to the EMM allocated portion

18   of the cost means that the total cost of a multi-jurisdictional allocated project must be

19   much greater than $5 million before EMM includes project documentation in its capital

20   budget docket filings. To illustrate this point, using Staff witness Alan J. Bax’s calculated



     1
         Ronald A. Klote Rebuttal Testimony Page 11, lines 20-21.


                                                        Page 4
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1    demand allocation factor2 of 0.5320 for the EMM retail jurisdiction in this case, 3 a project

2    would need to cost nearly $9.4 million in total before the EMM allocated portion of the

3    cost would reach $5 million. The cost threshold that Staff is recommending of $1 million

4    for the EMM allocated portion of the cost would be almost $1.9 million in total project

5    cost for a multi-jurisdictional allocated project.

6            In response to Staff Data Request 0516, EMM provided lists of projects for different

7    cost thresholds for projects that were placed in-service between June 1, 2022,

8    and June 30, 2026. The counts for the number of projects are summarized in the

9    table below.

10                                          Table 1: Total Project Counts

                                                                 Percentage of Projects
                     Projects Costing:                Count
                                                                 with EMM Allocation

                     Any EMM Allocation               16,5064               100%

                     $1 million (total)                 402                2.44%

                     $5 million (total)                  63                0.38%

11           In Staff Data Request 0516, Staff additionally requested the number of projects

12   that cost $1 million and $5 million for the EMM allocated portion of the cost.

13   In its response, EMM provided its proposed jurisdictional allocations by plant utility



     2
        The demand allocation factor is typically used for capital costs associated with generation and
     transmission plant, as well as certain operational and maintenance expenses.

       Alan J. Bax Direct Testimony Page 10, line 19.

       EMM provided the number of projects with any EMM allocated cost (i.e. projects with costs greater than
     $0) via email on September 9, 2026. EMM stated that 16,764 projects were placed in-service between
     June 1, 2022, and June 30, 2026, with 258 of those projects being blanket projects. Staff removed the
     blanket projects for this count.


                                                     Page 5
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1    account in lieu of the project counts. The lists of projects that cost $1 million

2    and $5 million in total provided in EMM’s response did not include the plant utility

3    account for each project, so Staff does not have sufficient information to calculate the

4    project counts itself. Staff has submitted follow-up Staff Data Request 0516.1 to request

5    the plant utility account for each of the projects so that Staff can determine the number

6    of projects that meet the cost thresholds for the EMM allocated portion of the cost.

7    This information will allow Staff to better illustrate the change in reporting volume when

8    comparing cost thresholds of $1 million and $5 million for the EMM allocated portion of

9    the cost.

10          With the information that Staff does have, the percentage of projects that

11   cost $1 million in total is 2.44% and the percentage of projects that cost $5 million in total

12   is 0.38%. The percentage of projects that cost $1 million in total is approximately 6.38

13   times more than the percentage of projects that cost $5 million in total, but still

14   represents a small fraction of EMM’s total projects. While this does not provide an exact

15   picture of the cost threshold changes that Staff is recommending, the proportion of

16   projects that cost $1 million in total to projects that cost $5 million in total is likely similar

17   to the proportion of projects that cost $1 million for the EMM allocated portion of the cost

18   to projects that cost $5 million for the EMM allocated portion of the cost.

19          Q.      How did Staff’s recommended modifications to the plant-in-service

20   reporting requirements consider the increased reporting volume?

21          A.      Staff’s recommendation changed the reporting frequency from annually to

22   quarterly. This would reduce the volume of documentation that EMM would need to file


                                                  Page 6
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1    at one time. The increased reporting frequency would also allow Staff to review

2    documentation on a more regular basis.

3            Staff’s recommendation also specified that the $1 million threshold be for the

4    EMM allocated portion of the cost rather than the total project cost. This should provide

5    clarity and address different interpretations of the cost threshold for plant-in-service

6    reporting requirements. This part of the recommendation also had the increased

7    reporting volume in mind as this allows for a higher total project cost for projects with

8    multi-jurisdictional cost allocation.

9            Q.      Do you agree with EMM witness Mr. Klote that Staff’s recommendation

10   substantially expands documentation that is included in the plant-in-service reporting?

11           A.      No. EMM witness Mr. Klote discusses the inclusion of purchase orders,

12   change orders, supporting documentation, attachments, and referenced documents

13   as significantly increasing the amount of effort and volume of reporting. 5,6

14   The ER-2022-0129 Stipulation plant-in-service reporting requirements already included

15   purchase orders and change orders. Therefore, the inclusion of purchase and change

16   orders represents no increase in the documentation required.

17           As discussed in my direct testimony, EMM’s capital budget docket filings did not

18   include documentation that was referenced in purchase and change orders. 7 This limits

19   Staff’s ability to effectively review EMM’s expenditures for these projects, including the




     5
       Ronald A. Klote Rebuttal Testimony Page 11, lines 14-15.
     6
       Ronald A. Klote Rebuttal Testimony Page 14, lines 19-23.
     7
       Trevor Rucker Direct Testimony Page 3, lines 3-8.


                                                      Page 7
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1    reasonableness and prudency of those expenditures. I also discussed this point in my

2    direct testimony.8

3               Staff expected that supporting, referenced, and attached documentation for

4    purchase and change orders would be included in EMM’s capital budget docket filings.

5    Therefore, Staff views this part of the recommendation as a clarification rather than

6    intending to increase the documentation reporting requirements.

7               Q.      Do you agree with EMM witness Mr. Klote’s discussion that clarification

8    regarding blanket projects may be necessary for the plant-in-service reporting

9    requirements?

10              A.      Yes. In the past, Staff has not expected that EMM would include blanket

11   projects for its plant-in-service reporting in its capital budget docket filings.

12   Therefore, it is reasonable to specify that projects that are part of a blanket project need

13   not be included.

14              OPC Rebuttal Testimony

15              Q.      Can you summarize the rebuttal testimony by OPC witness Dr. Marke?

16              A.      Yes. OPC witness Dr. Marke’s rebuttal testimony discussed costs

17   identified in my direct testimony for six game tables and game table accessories as part

18   of an Evergy building remodel. OPC witness Dr. Marke’s rebuttal testimony further

19   discussed that investments for recreational items such as the game tables should not be

20   included in rate base (which would earn a return on and require customers to pay for the




     8
         Trevor Rucker Direct Testimony Page 3, lines 11-17.


                                                        Page 8
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1    investment) and that there are more cost-effective alternatives to game tables. OPC

2    witness Dr. Marke recommends that all costs related to the game tables should be

3    disallowed from rate base.

4          Q.       Did your direct testimony include discussion of the specific game tables

5    procured by Evergy?

6          A.       No. At the time of my direct testimony, Staff had not received specific

7    information regarding the game tables and was awaiting a response to Staff Data Request

8    0449 to receive such information.

9          Q.       What information did Staff receive in response to Staff Data Request 0449?

10         A.       In response to Staff Data Request 0449, EMM provided the type, model, and

11   quantity of each game table, and the description and cost of accessories not included

12   with a game table. EMM did not have records of the costs of each individual game table,

13   but stated that one of each of following game tables were included:

14                 Plank & Hide Co Pool Table Morse Single Slate
15                 Plank & Hide Co Air Hockey
16                 Plank & Hide Co Shuffleboard
17                 Plank & Hide Co Ping Pong Table
18                 Plank & Hide Co Foosball Isaac Table
19                 Popa Shot Pro Dual Shot – Custom Graphics




                                              Page 9
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1            The total cost for the game tables was $48,177. EMM also provided that the

2    accessories (wood wall mounted pool cue rack, pool cues, three tabletop covers)

3    cost $4,389.43.9

4            Q.       What are the retail costs of the game tables?

5            A.       Staff contacted the manufacturer of the five Plank & Hide game tables

6    regarding the retail costs of the game tables. The manufacturer stated that they do not

7    sell directly to customers and directed Staff to an authorized dealer (Family Leisure)

8    in the Kansas City area. The authorized dealer’s website did not have information for all

9    of the game table models that were procured for Evergy’s building remodel. The pricing

10   information that Staff was able to find is as follows:

12                   Plank & Hide Co Air Hockey: Unknown
13                   Plank & Hide Co Shuffleboard: $6,942.33 11
14                   Plank & Hide Co Ping Pong Table: $3,749.00 12

16                   Popa Shot Pro Dual Shot – Custom Graphics: $1,199.99 14

                                                     Page 10
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1            Staff was unable to find any pricing information regarding a Plank & Hide Co air

2    hockey table, but adding up the pricing information for all of the other game tables results

3    in a total cost of $20,339.65,15 which is less than half of the $48,177 that was incurred by

4    Evergy for the game tables. Therefore, Staff concludes that Evergy selected expensive

5    game tables and also likely overpaid for the game tables.

6            Q.       What justification did EMM provide for the costs associated with the game

7    tables and game table accessories?

8            A.       As discussed by Dr. Marke, in response to Staff Data Request 0382,

9    EMM provided three main goals of the game tables: 1) Supporting Employee Mental

10   Health and Stress Reduction, 2) Improving Productivity and Work Quality, and

11   3) Promoting Physical Movement. EMM further stated “The inclusion of game tables in

12   designated break areas is a deliberate strategy to support employee well-being,

13   productivity, and overall workplace effectiveness. These amenities are part of a broader

14   approach to maintain a healthy, engaged, and high-performing workforce.”

15           Q.       Do you agree with OPC witness Dr. Marke that there are more cost-effective

16   alternatives to game tables to achieve the same goals that EMM provided as justification

17   for the game tables?

18           A.       Yes. OPC witness Dr. Marke listed multiple physical activities such as

19   outdoor walks or walking stairs as alternatives. I agree that EMM could allow employees



     15
        Staff notes that these costs only include the cost of the game tables, no other costs such as taxes or
     shipping were included, and that these costs are as of August 19, 2026, which may be different than those
     costs at the time of purchase of the game tables. Staff also notes that many of the game table retailers offer
     free shipping above a certain cost threshold that the game tables likely would have exceeded.


                                                       Page 11
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1    to participate in physical activities such as walks during their breaks that would support

2    the goals that EMM provided as justification for the game tables.

3           Q.     What are Staff’s conclusions regarding the costs incurred by EMM for the

4    game tables and game table accessories?

5           A.     Staff concludes that EMM selected expensive game tables and game table

6    accessories, EMM likely overpaid for these items, there are reasonable and more

7    cost-effective alternatives, and EMM did not provide justification that game tables are

8    more effective than the alternatives.


9    TRUE-UP DIRECT

10          Plant-in-Service Reporting Recommendation

11          Q.     Based on the above discussions, what does Staff now recommend to

12   the Commission?

13          A.     Staff recommends that the Commission order that Evergy Missouri Metro

14   quarterly file the following information and documentation in its capital budget docket

15   (Commission Case No. EO-2019-0047) for all projects (excluding projects that are part of

16   a blanket project) with an Evergy Missouri Metro jurisdictional cost over $1 million:

17                 a. Original project cost (total and EMM allocated),
18                 b. Final project cost (total and EMM allocated),
19                 c. In-service date,
20                 d. Project type,
21                 e. Project category,
22                 f. Project description,
23                 g. Project justification summary,


                                              Page 12
      Surrebuttal / True-Up Direct Testimony of
     Trevor Rucker


1                 h. Oversight reviews,
2                 i. Purchase orders (including supporting, attached, and referenced
3                     documentation), and
4                 j. Change orders (including supporting, attached, and referenced
5                     documentation).

6          Game Table Disallowance Recommendation

7          Q.     Do you have any recommendations for the Commission regarding the costs

8    associated with the game tables and game table accessories?

9          A.     Yes. Staff recommends that the costs for the game tables and game table

10   accessories be disallowed from EMM’s rate base. Staff witness Matthew R. Young will

11   incorporate this disallowance.


12   CONCLUSION

13         Q.     Can you summarize your surrebuttal / true-up direct testimony?

14         A.     Yes. In my surrebuttal / true-up direct testimony, I discussed 1) the rebuttal

15   testimony of EMM witnesses Ronald A. Klote and Ryan Mulvany regarding Staff’s

16   plant-in-service reporting recommendation, 2) the rebuttal testimony of the OPC witness

17   Geoff Marke regarding certain EMM expenditures, 3) Staff’s revised plant-in-service

18   reporting recommendation, and 4) Staff’s recommended disallowance of costs related

19   to game tables and game table accessories.

20         Q.     Does this conclude your surrebuttal / true-up direct testimony?

21         A.     Yes.
